input: Why is it enough to test divisors only up to the square root of n when checking if n is prime?
reference: If n = a * b then at least one factor is <= sqrt(n), so any composite n has a divisor at or below sqrt(n); finding none up to sqrt(n) proves n is prime. This makes the test O(sqrt(n)).

rubric.correctness: Correctly explains that a composite n must have a factor <= sqrt(n) (if n = a*b, one of a,b is <= sqrt(n)).
rubric.relevance: Directly answers the sqrt(n) question without drifting off-topic.
